title: Your Net Worth Is Fake — Real Number Is $127K Less
hook: Your net worth number might be wrong by six figures — and it's not your fault. The math behind the illusion is quietly wrecking your retirement plan.
angle: Exposes the three biggest miscalculations in how ordinary people track net worth: pre-tax retirement balances counted at face value, home equity that ignores selling costs, and cars treated as stable assets. Real accessible net worth is typically $100K–$150K lower than the headline number.
audience: Middle-class earners 28–55 who track net worth but have never stress-tested what the number actually means in real spending terms
key_numbers: 22–32% tax hit on every 401k dollar withdrawn
8–9% of home sale price lost to agent fees + closing costs
Average car loses $5,000 in year 1, $4,000 in year 2
$500K paper net worth → ~$370K real spendable value
Average gap: $127,000 between paper and real net worth
